configuration: The two contactABA cases of unittest/constrained-dynamics.cpp, 6D and 3D contact sets. The 6D case's empty-constraint-set prelude is not reproduced. All of them run on one frozen 28-joint humanoid with a free-flyer base, nq = 33, nv = 32, read from ic/<ic>/model.json, with every state operand, right-hand side and contact placement read from ic/<ic>/operands.json. Upstream draws a fresh random model per case; the frozen model replaces all of them, which loses no structural coverage because the sample-model builder always emits the same topology, joint types and joint names and varies only placements, inertias and limits.
observable: the joint acceleration contactABA returns under a proximal regularisation, and the accelerations and constraint forces of the two independent routes the case compares it against
default_vs_upstream: upstream, except that one frozen model replaces the per-case random draws and the frozen pools replace the per-case random right-hand sides and contact placements
variant: Two units in the last place, toward positive infinity, on fourteen active initial-condition numbers. Eleven are operands: one free-flyer orientation coordinate and one joint angle of each of the two frozen configurations (q[3], q[7], q2[3], q2[7]), the first velocity coordinate of each (v[0], v2[0]), the first acceleration coordinate of the first configuration (a[0]), and the first torque coordinate of each (tau[0], tau2[0]); two more are the first two entries of the frozen scalar pool (pool[0], pool[1]), which are the first two components of the right-hand sides a case draws. Three are model numbers, because the model is itself an initial-condition input and several graded quantities depend on it alone: the mass and the first lever component of the first body, and the leading rotation entry of the root joint's placement. That set follows the one the sibling rigid-body-algorithms leaf (PR #639) measured on this model, for the reasons it recorded: a joint angle alone is erased wherever a case overwrites the joint block of q; a free-flyer translation alone is inert, rigid-body dynamics being invariant under translation of the floating base; and no operand at all reaches a total mass. The root placement is perturbed because it is the one placement premultiplying the whole tree; its translation is zero and two ulps above zero is a subnormal, hence the rotation entry, whose two-ulp move leaves the matrix orthonormal far below any tolerance in this leaf. The frozen SE3 pool that supplies every contact placement is deliberately NOT perturbed: a rotation matrix is not a free scalar, and two ulps on one of its entries would pose a different problem rather than a perturbed one. Every graded value of this check moves between the two initial conditions.
altbuild: none: the same source built at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off reproduces the -O2 -DNDEBUG result bit-identically for this check, so an alternative build measures a floor of exactly zero and supplies no evidence. Measured on this host for all thirteen checks of the leaf. Eigen fixes the evaluation order of these expressions and the recursions are scalar, so the compiler has nothing to reassociate.

evidence.floor_how: The same official.cpp compiled twice against the same pinned source, once at -O2 -DNDEBUG and once at -O0 -ffp-contract=off, and run on ic/nominal; every graded value was bit-identical, so the measured floor is 0.0 and the bound is set from the variant spread and the physics instead. Repeated on the worker on 2026-09-14 (x86_64, inside the env image), result: bit-identical.

warrant: The graded quantities are the joint acceleration contactABA returns under a proximal regularisation, and the accelerations and constraint forces of the two independent routes the case compares it against. They are a joint acceleration in SI units in the model's own degree-of-freedom order and a constraint force in newtons and newton-metres in the order the constraint set declares. The bound is 0.0001 absolute plus 1e-06 relative, so on the largest graded magnitude here, about 203, it admits about 0.000303. This check's bound is four decades looser than the rest of the leaf, and the reason is in the case itself: upstream runs contactABA with a proximal parameter mu = 1e8 and ten sweeps, which adds a contact inertia of 1e8 at each contact joint. The articulated inertias are then dominated by that penalty and the returned acceleration is a difference of numbers eight decades larger than itself. Measured: the two-ulp variant moves the acceleration by 2.5e-07 on a value of 1.5e+01, an amplification of about 1e+08 relative to the input perturbation, which is mu. That is a property of the algorithm as the test configures it, not of this packaging, and a correct port would show the same amplification, so the bound has to contain it. The proximal loop contactABA runs stops on the floating-point comparison residual <= accuracy (constrained-dynamics.hxx), a discrete choice at Eigen's dummy precision, 1e-12, for the default-constructed settings this check uses; a port whose comparison flips and runs one sweep more or fewer differs by at most one sweep's update at the accuracy scale, 1e-12, which is under this bound. A fault a port can realistically make is many orders of magnitude larger than this bound: dropping a term of the constrained recursion, transposing a constraint Jacobian block, eliminating in the wrong frame, or mis-signing a cross product each move individual values by between 1e-2 and 1e+2 in these units. Measured on this host, a 0.1 per cent error injected into the largest graded value is rejected at 670 times the bound. The upstream identities also stay active: every BOOST_CHECK of every reproduced case runs unchanged, so such a fault is rejected twice over. It is achievable because the measured floor of this check is exactly zero -- the same source built at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off reproduces the -O2 result bit for bit -- and because the two-ulp variant moves the worst of the 210 graded values by 2.508e-07, using 0.00219 of the bound, that is 457 times of headroom. The bound is loose enough for a genuinely different implementation on another device and tight enough that no fault the upstream test is written to catch could pass it.
